X-13 Agent pool and offline-sold tickets

Bangla name: এজেন্ট pool ও অফলাইনে বিক্রি টিকিট

← 60 · Cross-cutting · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Agent pool. Seller agents (offline ticket sellers) have accounts in a fourth Cognito pool, Agent. Their only API records that pre-printed partner-sale tickets were sold, optionally with the buyer's phone number. No client in the five repositories signs in with the Agent pool or calls this API [UNCONFIRMED: Q-07].

2. Trigger and actor

Item Value
Actor Seller agent (account created in the admin portal, A-26)
Client Unknown [UNCONFIRMED: Q-07]
Cognito pool Agent
Role / program scope Backend adds role agent to tokens of this pool (X-14)

3. Business flow

  1. Partner tickets are generated for a partner reservation in the admin portal (A-11, A-12); their ticket type is Partner Sale.
  2. An agent sells some of them offline and records the sale with the ticket numbers (scanned QR or typed) and the buyer's phone/ID (max 20 characters).
  3. The platform refuses tickets that are not partner-sale tickets, that were already recorded, or whose event has passed its ticket-selling stop time.

4. Technical flow

# From → To Hop What happens
1 Agent client → Ticketing POST /ticketing/api/v1/offline-sold-ticket [HTTP + user token] (Agent pool) Policy = agent
2 Ticketing → database [Shared table] Reject numbers already in OfflineSoldTickets; load Tickets where TicketNumber in list and TicketType == "Partner Sale"; any missing → 400 "Invalid QR || …"
3 Ticketing → Event GET /event/api/v1/events/{eventId} per distinct event [HTTP + user token] (token forwarding) Reject if TicketSellingStopDateTime < UtcNow
4 Ticketing → database — Insert one OfflineSoldTickets row per ticket (UserId = agent's sub)

Kind Component
Service Ticketing: OfflineTicketSoldController → OfflineSoldTicketManager → TicketRepository, OfflineSoldTicketRepository; IEventClient
Service Event (event details)
AWS Cognito Agent pool

6. API contracts

Method Path Auth Request DTO Response Main errors (400)
POST /ticketing/api/v1/offline-sold-ticket Policy = agent OfflineSoldTicketCreateRequest { TicketNumbers: string[], TicketHolderIdentification?: string } { "message": "Offline sold tickets created successfully." } "The following ticket is already sold: …", "Invalid QR || This ticket can not be sold: …", "Phone no must not exceed 20 characters.", "Ticket requests are no longer available as the ticket selling period of … has ended." 
// POST /ticketing/api/v1/offline-sold-ticket
{ "ticketNumbers": ["BDI-000123", "BDI-000124"], "ticketHolderIdentification": "+8801711111111" }

// 200
{ "message": "Offline sold tickets created successfully." }

Ticket numbers above are illustrative of the shape; real numbers use the program's ticket prefix (A-03).

7. Data and side effects

One OfflineSoldTickets row per ticket (event, gallery/block/level, reservation id and public id, ticket number, holder id, agent id, CreatedAt). Nothing else changes: the ticket itself and its reservation are not updated.

9. Handover notes

  1. No known client. Neither portal nor app uses the Agent pool; the architecture document also lists the client as not found [UNCONFIRMED: Q-07].
  2. Agent account management is anonymous in the Admin service (X-05, X-18).
  3. No read API. Nothing in the backend reads OfflineSoldTickets back (no report, no admin screen) [UNCONFIRMED: Q-07].
  4. Token forwarding to Event: the Event endpoint has no [Authorize], so the forwarded Agent token is not checked there.

11. Developer test guide

Local testability: Partial. The endpoint and Agent-pool login work locally; no Partner Sale tickets and no agent-sold tickets are seeded (docs/local-dev.md §7, "What this does not cover"), so a successful call needs a partner reservation created first (A-11).
